vulnerabilities.weakness: A single product catalog replica is a hard dependency for checkout and can make purchases unavailable after one pod failure.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the productcatalogservice pod is killed, then checkout requests fail or become unavailable while the catalog has no healthy replica to serve them

vulnerabilities.weakness: The cart datastore has only one replica, so a pod failure can prevent cart-backed checkout and frontend cart operations.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the redis-cart pod is killed, then cart reads or writes fail during its recovery window and checkout cannot reliably retrieve carts

vulnerabilities.weakness: A single cartservice replica and its Redis dependency create a concentrated failure point on the checkout path.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the cartservice pod is killed, then checkout and frontend cart operations fail until the only instance is restored

vulnerabilities.weakness: Payment processing has a single replica and is a direct checkout dependency, creating an immediate revenue-impacting outage risk.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the paymentservice pod is killed, then checkout attempts requiring payment fail until the sole payment instance returns

vulnerabilities.weakness: The checkout orchestrator has one replica and synchronously depends on six single-replica services, concentrating checkout availability risk.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the checkoutservice pod is killed, then frontend checkout requests fail because no checkout replica remains to orchestrate the transaction

vulnerabilities.weakness: The sole entrypoint replica is a single point of failure for all user traffic.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the frontend pod is killed, then users cannot reach catalog, cart, or checkout functionality until the only entrypoint instance returns

vulnerabilities.weakness: The optional advertising service has one replica, but its isolated failure should be degradable to a frontend without advertisements.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the adservice pod is killed, then the frontend continues serving core pages without advertisements rather than checkout becoming unavailable

vulnerabilities.weakness: The non-checkout recommendation service has one replica, but its failure should degrade recommendations without blocking purchases.
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the recommendationservice pod is killed, then the frontend omits or degrades recommendations while core browsing and checkout remain available

systemic: Every service has replicas set to 1, so a pod failure removes all capacity for that service until recovery.
Every service has pdb set to false, so voluntary disruption protection is absent across the architecture.
Every service has hpa set to false, so services cannot automatically add capacity during load or recovery.
All services have readiness_probe and liveness_probe enabled, but these facts do not establish that probes detect dependency failure or prevent failed requests from reaching the service.
blind_spots: Timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, fallbacks, and failure propagation inside service code are not shown.
The facts do not show whether checkout can complete when email, currency, shipping, or catalog calls fail.
Pod scheduling topology, anti-affinity, node failure behavior, and disruption timing are not shown.
Persistent volume availability, Redis replication, backup, and data recovery behavior are not shown.
Resource limit values and CPU or memory utilization are not shown, so throttling and out-of-memory risk cannot be assessed.
Probe thresholds, startup behavior, and whether probes exercise real dependencies are not shown.
